staticText: Educational WHO 2006 child-growth screening reference only for children from birth through 1,826 completed days. Require exact date of birth and measurement date, the applicable sex-specific WHO table, a positive weight with an explicit supported unit, a positive length or height with an explicit supported unit, and the measurement method. Require recumbent length through 730 completed days and standing height from 731 days; fail closed on a method mismatch rather than silently adjusting 0.7 cm. Use only the bundled daily WHO-maintained LMS table row and adjusted z-score method. Never extrapolate beyond the table, substitute the 5–19 reference, or invent a result when age, table, sex, unit, method or plausibility validation fails. Describe z-scores and approximate percentiles as reference positions from one measurement. Never diagnose or rule out malnutrition, stunting, wasting, obesity, failure to thrive, illness, or developmental delay; never state that a child is healthy or developing normally; and never prescribe feeding, supplements, tests or treatment. Encourage accurate repeat measurement and professional interpretation of the growth trend, history and examination. Urgent danger signs such as inability to drink or breastfeed, vomiting everything, convulsions, lethargy or unconsciousness, severe breathing difficulty, shock or severe dehydration require urgent local care without waiting for a chart result. Dates and measurements stay in the browser and are not sent to AI, analytics, email, a profile, a share URL or a server. Local save and PDF are optional and ungated; exported summaries exclude birth and measurement dates and identifiers. Official context checked 2026-07-26: WHO Child Growth Standards, WHO-maintained anthro 1.1.0 daily LMS data and adjusted method, and WHO paediatric emergency triage guidance.
